purpose: Track why public sources are especially weak for tradition-axis material.

biases.effect: Overrepresents communities with English public-facing resources.
biases.mitigation: Seek multilingual and community-authored review before public release.

biases.effect: Clergy or organizational pages may underrepresent family, lay, regional, caste, class, gender, or diaspora practice.
biases.mitigation: Add consented family/practitioner testimony only after review.

biases.effect: Commercial pages may simplify practice for arrangement logistics.
biases.mitigation: Tag as low weight and do not use for authority.

biases.effect: Rare phenomena such as tukdam may be framed for scientific curiosity rather than sacred relation.
biases.mitigation: Use non-extraction rules and tradition authority gates.

biases.effect: A page being public can be mistaken for permission to reproduce or teach.
biases.mitigation: Treat publicness as discoverability only, not authorization.
